bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar has 10 operational sugar mills, 5 more to start soon, says CM Samrat Choudhary as ...
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News Top News Trendings Bihar CM Samrat Choudhary flags off 'Ganna Vikas Rath-2026' (Photo: x/@samrat4bjp) Patna (Bihar): Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Chaudhary on Tuesday launched the ‘Ganna Vikas Rath-2026’–an initiative organised by the Sugarcane Industries Department, Government of Bihar–from a stage in front of the ‘Samvad Kaksh’ at the Chief Minister’s Secretariat. The Chief Minister flagged off the ‘Sugarcane Development Chariots’ for all districts. According to an official release from the Bihar Chief Minister’s Office, on this occasion, the Chief Minister stated that the prosperity of sugarcane farmers, an increase in sugarcane production, and elevating the sugar industry to new heights are top priorities for the state government. Currently, 10 sugar mills are operational in the state, and 5 more are set to begin operations soon. He added that this campaign, launched with the vision of a “Prosperous Industry, Empowered Bihar,” will play a crucial role in bringing information about modern technology, scientific farming, and government schemes directly to the farmers. The sugar industry in Bihar will be strengthened through the establishment of new sugar mills and the revival of closed, defunct ones. Sugarcane cultivation is not only a vital means of increasing farmers’ income but will also bolster the rural economy and create new employment opportunities. The Chief Minister expressed confidence that the ‘Sugarcane Development Chariot-2026’ (Ganna Vikas Rath-2026) will connect farmers with modern technology and government schemes, while also providing a new direction for the growth of sugarcane production and the sugar industry in Bihar, a release said. Through this ‘Sugarcane Development Chariot,’ farmers will be provided with information on improved sugarcane varieties, scientific farming practices, organic fertilizers, and modern agricultural techniques. Farmers will also be made aware of subsidies available for agricultural machinery under the ‘Sugarcane Mechanisation Scheme’ and for certified sugarcane seeds under the ‘Chief Minister’s Sugarcane Development Programme.’ Furthermore, information regarding the availability of free sugarcane seeds to encourage cultivation in new areas will be shared. Digital technology is being leveraged to provide farmers with more convenient and accessible services; initiatives have been launched to connect them to digital platforms through the ‘Ganna ID’ (Sugarcane ID) and the ‘Ganna Sathi’ (Sugarcane Companion) AI chatbot. Additionally, awareness and public participation will be fostered among farmers through agricultural workshops and street plays. Present on this occasion were Deputy Chief Ministers Vijay Kumar Chaudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav, Minister for the Sugar Industry Sanjay Kumar, Chief Secretary Pratyaya Amrit, Secretaries to the Chief Minister Lokesh Kumar Singh and Sanjay Kumar Singh, Secretary of the Sugar Industry Department Dharmendra Singh, and other senior officials, a release added. (ANI)

bihar_raw_news.title: Nitish Setu: Bihar's six-lane Ganga bridge sparks credit war ahead of launch by PM
bihar_raw_news.content: SIGN IN Edition IN IN US Download App Follow Us On: News India Nitish Setu: Bihar’s six-lane Ganga bridge sparks credit war ahead of launch by PM Nitish Setu: Bihar's six-lane Ganga bridge sparks credit war ahead of launch by PM Bihar's 19.76-km Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur six-lane bridge, named Nitish Setu, will be inaugurated by PM Narendra Modi on Saturday, November 21. However, its naming after former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar has triggered a political row, with the RJD questioning the decision and demanding an alternative name. Advertisement All you need to know about Bihar's new six-lane Ganga bridge, Nitish Setu (Photo: X) By: Rohit Kumar Singh Patna , Nov 17, 2026 19:42 IST Last Updated Nov 17, 2026 19:42 IST Published by Priyanka Kumari Nov 17, 2026 19:38 IST Edited by Priyanka Kumari Bihar is set to get a major infrastructure boost with the inauguration of the Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur six-lane bridge over the Ganga, now named Nitish Setu. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to inaugurate the 19.76-km project on November 21, 2026, opening up a new road link between Patna and north Bihar. Connecting Kachchi Dargah in Patna district to Bidupur in Vaishali district through Raghopur Diara, the bridge is expected to ease travel across the Ganga, reduce congestion on existing routes and improve connectivity for thousands of commuters. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story But the project is also making headlines for a political reason. The Bihar government's decision to name the bridge after former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar has triggered a war of words between the ruling JD(U)-BJP camp and the opposition RJD, bringing the project's history and political credit into focus. Here is a look at the bridge's route, cost, construction, significance and the controversy surrounding its name. HOW LONG IS THE BRIDGE, AND THE PLACES IT CONNECTS The Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur project stretches 19.76 km, comprising a 9.76-km main bridge over the Ganga and 10 km of approach roads. The six-lane bridge connects NH-30 near Kachchi Dargah in Patna district with NH-103 near Bidupur in Vaishali district. Its route passes through Raghopur Diara, an area that has long struggled with connectivity because of its geographical location amid river channels. Built using an extradosed cable-stayed design, the bridge is 32 metres wide, with spans of up to 150 metres between its main supporting pillars. The engineering design uses cables to support the bridge structure, allowing longer distances between pillars. The project is being implemented by the Bihar State Road Development Corporation Limited (BSRDCL). Larsen & Toubro (L&T) and South Korean company Daewoo jointly undertook its construction. WHAT IS THE PROJECT COST AND WHO FUNDED IT? The total approved cost of the project stands at Rs 4,988.40 crore, according to the Bihar government's project document. This includes Rs 696.60 crore earmarked for land acquisition. The project received financial assistance from the Asian Development Bank (ADB), alongside funding from the Bihar government. ADB approved assistance of USD 450.84 million, with the funding shared between the bank and the state

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Plans Two New Sugar Mills in Motipur and Saran - Drishti IAS
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar Prev Next Bihar Plans Two New Sugar Mills in Motipur and Saran 17 Nov 2026 2 min read Why in News? The Bihar government has proposed setting up two new sugar mills at Motipur (Muzaffarpur) and Taraiya (Saran), and the preparation of their Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) has been initiated. Key Points DPR Preparation: Separate DPRs will assess the technical and financial feasibility, resource requirements and estimated costs of both mills. Benefits to Sugarcane Farmers: Nearby sugar mills will provide farmers with easier access to facilities for selling sugarcane. They may reduce transportation costs and facilitate sugarcane supply. Employment Generation: The proposed mills are expected to generate direct and indirect employment through mill operations and related activities. Economic Significance: The projects are expected to support sugarcane cultivation, strengthen the rural economy and contribute to the revival of Bihar's sugar industry. Sugarcane Production in Bihar Importance: Sugarcane is an important cash crop of Bihar and a major raw material for the sugar and agro-based industries. Major Producing Areas: Sugarcane cultivation is concentrated mainly in West Champaran, East Champaran, Gopalganj, Sitamarhi, Siwan and Samastipur. West Champaran is a major producing district. Sugar Industry: Bihar has a long history of sugar production. The first sugar mill in Bihar was established at Marhowrah (Saran) in 1904. Research: The ICAR–Indian Sugarcane Research Institute's Regional Centre at Motipur, Muzaffarpur, works on improved varieties and cultivation practices. Government Initiative: The Mukhyamantri Ganna Vikas Yojana promotes improved sugarcane cultivation through quality seeds, subsidies and modern farming practices. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar To Start Evening Classes for Academically Weak Students in Classes 9 to 12
bihar_raw_news.content: Bihar To Start Evening Classes for Academically Weak Students in Classes 9 to 12 By Sahil Behl Last Updated: Nov 17, 2026, 15:28 IST Bihar will introduce free evening classes under the Sankalp Sandhya programme for academically weak and economically disadvantaged students of Classes 9 to 12 from November 17. Classes will run from 5 pm to 7:30 pm until March 31, 2027, across selected government schools in all 38 district headquarters. Bihar To Start Evening Classes for Academically Weak Students in Classes 9 to 12 Register for Result Updates The Bihar Education Department has launched a special evening-class programme, ‘Sankalp Sandhya’, to provide additional academic support to students who are struggling with their studies. The initiative will cover students of Classes 9 to 12 studying in government schools across all 38 district headquarters of the state. The evening classes will begin on November 17, 2026, and continue until March 31, 2027. The programme will focus on students who need extra help in their studies, particularly those from economically weaker backgrounds. The classes will be conducted free of cost to help students improve their understanding of important subjects and prepare for upcoming examinations. According to the directions issued by the Education Department, each district headquarters will have at least one and a maximum of three government schools selected for the programme. “The necessary infrastructure available in government schools located in the 38 district headquarters of the state can be utilized for the Evening Classes under “Sankalp Sandhya”,” the directorate’s instructions stated. Sankalp Sandhya: Class Timings and Subjects Under the programme, evening classes will be conducted daily from 5 pm to 7:30 pm. Students will receive additional lessons in five subjects, including: English Mathematics Science Computer Science Artificial Intelligence (AI) The schools will use their existing facilities, including smart boards and other digital infrastructure, to conduct these classes. The additional sessions will also help students complete their homework, clear doubts and prepare for examinations. Teachers to Receive Additional Incentives Government school teachers will be involved in conducting the evening classes. Teachers assigned to the programme will be eligible for one compensatory leave for every three days of work. They will also receive an additional honorarium or incentive for taking these classes. Schools can also involve retired teachers and volunteers to support the initiative. Retired officers below 70 years of age from the Indian Administrative Service (IAS), Bihar Administrative Service (BAS), Bihar Education Service (BES) and other government services can also volunteer to teach students. However, retired officers will have to obtain temporary permission from the District Education Officer (DEO) before joining the programme. They will not receive any honorarium for their voluntary teaching services. Who Will Monitor the Evening Classes? The programme will operate under the supervision of the respective District Education Officers. District Magistrates will also provide necessary guidance and issue instructions regarding its implementation. School principals have been asked to make arrangements for the classes and maintain records of participating students, including their names, classes, subjects and mobile numbers.

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar initiates 'Detailed Project Reports' process for proposed sugar mills in Muzaffarpur and Saran
bihar_raw_news.content: All News English Indian Sugar News Sugar News AI Representational Image Bihar has stepped up efforts to revive its sugar industry, initiating the preparation of Detailed Project Reports (DPRs) for two proposed sugar mills in Muzaffarpur and Saran districts, Patna Press reported. The proposed units will be located in Motipur in Muzaffarpur and Taraiya in Saran. Following directions from the state government, the Sugarcane Industries Department has written to the selected agency, assigning it the task of preparing DPRs for both projects. The reports will assess the feasibility of setting up the mills, including resource availability, investment requirements, estimated project costs and other essential aspects. Their findings will help determine the next steps towards establishing the proposed facilities. The projects are expected to benefit sugarcane farmers in the two districts and neighbouring areas by providing access to processing facilities closer to their fields. This could improve market access for growers and reduce the transportation costs associated with supplying cane to mills farther away. The proposed units could also generate direct and indirect employment in manufacturing, transportation, logistics and related activities, while supporting local businesses and economic activity in the surrounding rural areas. With the DPR preparation process initiated for Motipur and Taraiya, the proposed projects have entered the feasibility assessment stage. Their implementation will depend on the findings of the reports and subsequent government decisions.

bihar_raw_news.content: He raised over Rs 9 lakh to build a computer lab in Bihar; Meet Sumair Kandhari, whose initiative has reached 1,700 students and 750 women Sumair Kandhari's Pathways Plus is bridging Bihar's digital divide by teaching computer skills, Python and AI, reaching over 1,700 students and 750 women. Sheetal Kumari November 17, 2026 / 12:01 IST (Representative Image: Canva) Pathways Plus bridges digital divides for rural Bihar students. The initiative offers computer training, Python, and AI lessons. Over 1,700 students and 750 women have benefited so far. Did our AI summary help? Market Mastery Webinar by Vishal Malkan Find the weak links in your portfolio by Vishal Malkan Register for FREE Webinar Register for FREE A lack of access to computers continues to limit learning opportunities for children in several rural communities, even as technology becomes increasingly important in education and employment. Sumair Kandhari is working to bridge this gap in Bihar through Pathways Plus, a digital education initiative launched in 2023 that provides computer training, programming lessons and exposure to artificial intelligence (AI) to underserved students. The programme has reached more than 1,700 students and 750 women, according to the Diana Award's 2026 Roll of Honour. Developed in partnership with KCS Foundation India, Pathways Plus focuses on making digital learning accessible to children who have limited opportunities to use computers. The initiative combines fundraising, curriculum development and teacher training to create a sustainable learning environment. It began with the establishment of a computer laboratory in Samastipur, Bihar, and has since expanded its reach through a structured training programme. Sumair Kandhari's journey: A teacher's influence behind Pathways Plus Sumair's interest in improving access to education was shaped by his mathematics teacher, Dr Pankaj Jha. Stories shared by Jha about his upbringing in Bihar and his commitment to making education accessible encouraged Sumair to consider how technology could improve learning opportunities for children in underserved areas. He realised that access to the internet alone could not bridge the digital divide. Students also needed computers, practical training and guidance to understand how technology could be used for learning and future opportunities. With this objective, Sumair started working on Pathways Plus in 2023. He raised approximately $10,000 to establish a computer laboratory featuring 20 workstations in Samastipur. KCS Foundation India partnered with him to develop the project and connect it with the local community. bihar_raw_news.title: NFR's North-East network goes fully electric in less than a decade | MorungExpress
bihar_raw_news.content: Langting railway station in Assam, with overhead electrification infrastructure in place. On November 17, NFR announces 100% railway electrification across its jurisdiction in North-East within a decade. (Photo Courtesy: NFR CPRO) North-East 17th November 2026 Maligaon, November 17 (MExN): In what was officially described as an “extraordinary achievement,” the Northeast Frontier Railway (NFR) has recorded 100% railway electrification across its jurisdiction in North-East India in less than 10 years. According to an NFR release, there was no railway electrification in the region prior to 2014 and the initiative began in 2017-18 as part of efforts to modernise railway infrastructure and promote energy-efficient transportation. All active railway sections across the NE states under NFR have now been electrified, it added. As per cumulative figures up to 2026-27, NFR has electrified 4,311.96 route kilometres (RKM) across its jurisdiction. Assam accounts for the largest share at 2,546.04 RKM, followed by West Bengal with 987.51 RKM and Bihar with 427.49 RKM. The remaining electrified sections include Tripura (269.45 RKM), Mizoram (52.88 RKM), Arunachal Pradesh (11.67 RKM), Meghalaya (9.58 RKM), Nagaland (6 RKM) and Manipur (1.35 RKM). Year-wise figures show that NFR electrified 915.62 RKM in 2023-24 and 1,141.38 RKM in 2024-25. A further 445.66 RKM was electrified in 2025-26, while 141.77 RKM has been recorded so far in 2026-27. More recently, electrification was completed in the Lumding–Badarpur section on September 14, 2026, and the Bairabi–Sairang section in Mizoram on October 12. Electrification work is also progressing alongside ongoing new railway line projects to ensure that upcoming infrastructure is equipped with modern traction systems. NFR said the achievement reaffirmed its commitment to modernising railway infrastructure and promoting energy-efficient and greener transportation, in line with Indian Railways’ vision of achieving 100% electrification of its broad-gauge network.

bihar_raw_news.title: Khesari Lal Yadav backs naming of bridge after Nitish Kumar; says no need for controversy
bihar_raw_news.content: Khesari Lal Yadav backs naming of bridge after Nitish Kumar; says no need for controversy IANS Update: 2026-11-17 15:30 IST Chief Minister Nitish Kumar Patna: Bhojpuri actor and singer, Khesari Lal Yadav, has supported the Bihar government's decision to rename the Kachchi Dargah-Bidupur six-lane bridge as 'Nitish Setu', saying there is no need for a controversy over the issue as both Nitish Kumar and Lalu Prasad have made significant contributions to the state. The controversy intensified after Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary announced that the bridge would be named after former Chief Minister Nitish Kumar. Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to visit Bihar on November 21 to inaugurate two major projects, including an industrial area in Hajipur and the Nitish Setu. Reacting to the debate, Khesari Lal said both Nitish Kumar and RJD President, Lalu Prasad, were equally respected and loved by the people of Bihar. He said his personal opinion would not make any difference, as people were well-aware of the contributions made by the two leaders. "Nitish Kumar is as dear to us as Lalu Chacha (Lalu Prasad Yadav). Both have been associated with each other for a long time. They have worked and struggled for the people, and their contributions are known to everyone," he said. Khesari Lal added that since both leaders had worked for public welfare, there was no reason to turn the naming of the bridge into a political controversy. "What is happening is fine. The bridge is being named after someone from among our own people," he remarked. Meanwhile, the proposed renaming has drawn sharp criticism from the RJD leadership. Rohini Acharya questioned the government's decision in a post on X, suggesting that the bridge, located in the Raghopur area, should instead be named 'Samajik Nyay Setu (Social Justice Bridge)' or after Lalu Prasad. She also praised the contributions of her father and expressed displeasure over the government's move. Leader of the Opposition Tejashwi Yadav also attacked the BJP over the decision. He alleged that the BJP had effectively sidelined Nitish Kumar while he was still alive, adding that public infrastructure is generally named after people who are no longer alive. The debate over the bridge's name has now emerged as another political flashpoint between the ruling NDA and the Opposition in Bihar. national_raw_news.title: PM Modi calls for setting concrete goals to strengthen cooperation among Quad members
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today described the Quad as a constructive and trusted partnership and called for setting concrete goals to strengthen cooperation among the four member countries in the next phase. Addressing the Quad meeting in Manila, PM Modi highlighted the historic association between the city of Manila and the grouping, noting that officials from the four countries first met here in 2007. He said Manila also hosted the revival of the Quad dialogue in 2017, making the latest meeting an important milestone in the partnership. He said that holding a Quad meeting once again at this historic city marks an important milestone. The Prime Minister also pointed to the continued high-level engagement among the member countries, stating that their foreign ministers had met five times since January last year, reflecting their political will and shared commitment to the partnership. Highlighting India’s approach towards the grouping, PM Modi said the Quad was a constructive and trusted partnership that aimed to deliver practical solutions for the entire Indo-Pacific region. He said cooperation among the four countries covered a wide range of areas, including maritime security, trusted supply chains, emerging technologies and disaster response. He said that it has been India’s endeavour that the Quad provides trusted solutions for the entire Indo-Pacific.

national_raw_news.title: PM Modi calls for greater India-ASEAN cooperation to ensure peace and stability in Indo-Pacific
national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi today highlighted the growing partnership between India and ASEAN and called for greater cooperation to ensure peace, stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific region. He was addressing the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit in Manila, Philippines. Addressing the summit, Prime Minister Modi congratulated Philippine President Ferdinand Marcos Jr. on his successful chairship of ASEAN and his important contribution as country coordinator for India. He said that this was his 13th interaction with ASEAN leaders in this format and said India’s Act East policy had given India-ASEAN relations new momentum and depth over the past several years. Highlighting the expansion of bilateral cooperation, PM Modi said the partnership, built on shared culture and heritage, was now expanding into new areas such as digital technologies, defence and space. He further stated that since 2014, India and ASEAN had undertaken more than 100 initiatives to strengthen people-to-people ties. More than 250 quick-impact projects had been launched, while over 10,000 scholarships had been provided for skill development. The Prime Minister also highlighted that direct flights between India and nine ASEAN countries, along with growing tourism, reflected the close ties between the two sides. Referring to the global situation, PM Modi observed that the world had faced one crisis after another over the past few years, making peace, stability and predictability increasingly important. He said the summit’s theme, “Navigating Our Future Together,” held particular significance in the current global context. He emphasised that India and ASEAN together represented about one-fourth of the world’s population and that their future should be shaped through cooperation rather than competition. He added that India and ASEAN possessed the capabilities and shared resolve to make the region a symbol of peace and stability. PM Modi also noted that this was his third visit to an ASEAN country this year, reflecting the special importance ASEAN held for India. He said India’s development and ASEAN’s prosperity were closely interconnected, adding that the ASEAN Community Vision 2045 and India’s vision of Viksit Bharat by 2047 could play an important role in achieving shared aspirations. The Prime Minister observed that over the past twelve years, India and ASEAN had given their partnership fresh momentum and stressed the need to work together to chart a new course for the future of the region. Reaffirming India’s commitment, PM Modi said the country’s support for ASEAN unity and ASEAN centrality would remain unwavering. Expressing confidence in the outcome of the summit, he said the meeting would elevate the Comprehensive Strategic Partnership to new heights and contribute to building a secure, inclusive and prosperous Indo-Pacific. Earlier, PM Modi visited the Khalsa Diwan Gurudwara in Manila and led the foundation-stone laying ceremony for its redevelopment in the presence of the Panch Pyare.

national_raw_news.content: The ASEAN member states and India today agreed to strengthen cooperation in disaster management, with a focus on early warning systems, emergency response, disaster preparedness and resilient recovery. The agreement was reached at the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit in Manila, where both sides adopted the ASEAN-India Joint Statement on Cooperation in Disaster Management, seeking to enhance regional coordination and build resilience against natural disasters. Recognising the shared vulnerability of ASEAN countries and India to earthquakes, tsunamis, floods, cyclones, extreme heat and landslides, the two sides stressed the importance of timely humanitarian assistance, effective disaster response mechanisms and stronger regional cooperation. Under the joint statement, ASEAN and India will strengthen coordination among their disaster management agencies, including the ASEAN Committee on Disaster Management (ACDM), the AHA Centre and India’s National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA). They will also expand cooperation on early warning systems through the exchange of satellite data, seismic information and meteorological forecasts. Both sides agreed to conduct joint training programmes, simulation exercises and exchanges of disaster response personnel to improve preparedness and rapid response capabilities. They will also facilitate humanitarian assistance and disaster relief to affected countries upon request or with their consent. The agreement also focuses on sustainable post-disaster recovery, resilient infrastructure and capacity building, with particular attention to women, youth, older persons and persons with disabilities. ASEAN and India will further explore the use of artificial intelligence, machine learning and big data analytics in disaster risk assessment, early warning and response coordination. Relevant ASEAN bodies and their Indian counterparts will identify specific activities to implement the joint statement under the ASEAN-India Plan of Action (2026-2030) and monitor progress through existing mechanisms. The initiative aims to strengthen regional preparedness, improve coordination during emergencies and enhance the resilience of communities across ASEAN and India.

national_raw_news.title: India’s electronics exports grow 44% to $32 bn in six months this fiscal 8 mins ago 6
national_raw_news.content: India’s electronic goods exports registered strong growth of 44 per cent during April-September this fiscal year, increasing from over 22 billion dollars in the corresponding period of 2025-26 to around 32 billion dollars. While smartphones continued to account for the largest share of the electronics export basket, non-smartphone electronics recorded significantly faster growth, reflecting the broadening and diversification of India’s electronics exports across components, printed circuit boards, communication equipment, memory products and storage devices. Exports of smartphones increased by over 35 per cent, from 13 billion dollars in April-September last year to over 18 billion dollars during April-September this year. Smartphones continued to be the largest component of India’s electronic goods exports. However, their share in total electronic goods exports moderated from 60.3 per cent to 56.8 per cent, amid faster growth in other electronics segments. Non-smartphone electronics exports recorded a growth of over 56 per cent, increasing from around nine billion dollars to over 13 billion dollars during the period. The share of non-smartphone electronics in total electronic goods exports increased from 39.7 per cent to 43.2 per cent, indicating a broadening of India’s electronics export basket. Exports of parts and accessories comprising mounted printed circuit boards increased from over 63 million dollars to over two billion dollars registering growth of 3219 per cent. Singapore was the leading destination, with exports reaching 1.87 billion dollars, followed by China at 111.5 million dollars.

national_raw_news.title: UP SIR: Draft roll published for correction till 16th Dec 2 hours ago 39
national_raw_news.content: The draft electoral roll under the Special Summary Revision 2027 published in Uttar Pradesh today, with claims and objections to be accepted from November 17 to December 16. According to the list state’s electorate has increased by around 18.84 lakh since the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. As per the draft electoral roll for the Special Summary Revision (SSR) 2027, the state’s total number electorate is 13 crore 58 lakh 68 thousand and 905. The number of male voters rose by 7.87 lakh to 7 crore 38 lakh 58 thousand and 510 while female electors increased by nearly 10.97 lakh to 6 crore 20 lakh 6 thousand and 353. Chief Electoral Officer Navdeep Rinwa said that the claims and objections can be filed from today to 16th next month. The disposal of claims and objections is scheduled to be completed by December 28, with the final electoral roll set to be published on January 4, 2027. He said that as part of the exercise, special camps will be organised at polling stations across the state on 21, 22, 28 and 29 of this month. Booth Level Officers (BLOs) will remain present with draft electoral rolls and application forms to assist voters. Electors can use Form 6 for fresh registration, Form 6A for eligible overseas Indian electors, Form 7 for objections or deletion requests, and Form 8 for corrections, change of address, replacement of EPIC cards and marking of persons with disabilities.

national_raw_news.title: Logo and mascot for 8th edition of Khelo India Youth Games unveiled 15 Nov 2026 | 6:18 PM 350
national_raw_news.content: Youth Affairs and Sports Minister Dr Mansukh Mandaviya and Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy today unveiled the logo and mascot for the 8th edition of the Khelo India Youth Games. The Games will be held across six cities in Telangana from 11th to 22nd of next month. Addressing the gathering, Dr Mandaviya said Prime Minister Narendra Modi has placed special emphasis on connecting the youth with sports and making sports an integral part of the country’s development vision. He said various sporting events, including the Khelo India Youth Games, Khelo India Beach Games, Winter Games and Tribal Games, are being organised under the Khelo India initiative to encourage greater participation of young people in sports. Speaking on the occasion, Telangana Chief Minister A. Revanth Reddy said events such as the Khelo India Youth Games would help advance the Prime Minister’s vision of a Nasha Mukt Yuva for Viksit Bharat by encouraging young people to stay away from substance abuse and other social challenges. Both Dr Mandaviya and Mr Reddy expressed their gratitude to Prime Minister Narendra Modi for his guidance and support in organising the Khelo India Youth Games in Telangana. The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports said around eight thousand athletes and participants are expected to take part in the Games. The 8th edition will feature 29 disciplines, including 27 competitive sports and two demonstration events.

national_raw_news.title: Higher education sector witnesses significant growth over 12 yrs, says VP Radhakrishnan 16 Nov 2026 | 9:16 PM 60
national_raw_news.content: Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan today said India’s higher education sector has witnessed significant expansion over the past twelve years, with a substantial increase in educational institutions and student enrollment. Addressing an event in Cuttack today, he said the number of universities in the country has increased from 760 in 2014-15 to over 1,400 at present. The number of IITs has gone up from 16 to 23, IIMs from 13 to 22, and AIIMS from seven to 20. The Vice-President said higher education enrolment has also increased from 3.42 crore to over 4.5 crore students. Referring to Odisha’s sizeable tribal population, he urged universities to introduce school-connect programmes to encourage tribal children to pursue higher education and prevent dropouts. Calling upon students to uphold the principle of ‘Nation First – Rashtra Pratham’, he emphasised the importance of knowledge, character and compassion. He also urged young people to stay away from drugs and embrace the message of ‘No to Drugs’. Vice-President CP Radhakrishnan today also inaugurated an orientation programme for members of the 17th Odisha Legislative Assembly in Bhubaneswar. The programme aimed to strengthen the legislative understanding and parliamentary skills of newly elected members by familiarising them with parliamentary traditions, legislative procedures and the functioning of the House. Addressing the legislators, the Vice-President emphasised the importance of informed debate, constructive discussions and meaningful participation in the legislative process.

national_raw_news.title: Leading through the storm: How India managed its COVID-19 response
national_raw_news.content: India’s response to the COVID-19 pandemic was shaped by a series of timely decisions, clear responsibilities and continuous adjustments as the public health situation evolved. From airport screening and inter-ministerial coordination before the first reported case to emergency healthcare measures, oxygen allocation and a nationwide vaccination campaign, the Government’s approach combined central direction with implementation by States and local authorities. The response, which extended from January 2020 to May 2023, involved government institutions, healthcare workers, laboratories, private hospitals, industry and civil society. Its central features were early risk assessment, legal and administrative coordination, evidence-based decisions, mobilisation of resources and sustained public health action. As of 31 December 2025, 97 per cent of the population aged 12 years and above had received at least one dose of a COVID-19 vaccine, while 90 per cent was fully vaccinated. A total of 22.89 crore precaution doses had also been administered across the country. The challenge: Responding to an unfamiliar virus The World Health Organization (WHO) was notified on 31 December 2019 about pneumonia cases of unknown cause in Wuhan, China. With no vaccine, established treatment or comprehensive understanding of the virus available at the time, countries faced the challenge of preparing for a rapidly evolving health emergency. For India, the immediate concern was the possibility of imported infections through international travel. The Government began assessing risks, strengthening surveillance and coordinating with different ministries even before the country’s first reported case. India’s first COVID-19 case was reported in Thrissur, Kerala, on 30 January 2020. By then, airport screening, monitoring arrangements and initial preparedness measures were already underway. The response subsequently moved through five broad phases: preparation, containment, phased reopening, vaccination and surge management, followed by sustained health-system preparedness and adaptation. Early preparedness: Acting before the first case India’s initial response focused on anticipating the threat and creating mechanisms to identify and manage suspected infections. The Joint Monitoring Group (JMG), a standing technical forum comprising health officials and experts and chaired by the Director General of Health Services, met on 8 January 2020 to assess the emerging risk and review preparedness. International passenger screening began on 17 January and was extended to 21 airports within a week. On 25 January, seven multidisciplinary Central teams were deputed to review airport screening arrangements and assess the end-to-end management of suspected cases referred to designated hospitals. The Health Ministry also wrote to four other ministries, while the Cabinet Secretariat convened inter-ministerial meetings to coordinate preparations. A national operations centre, managed by the National Centre for Disease Control (NCDC), was activated on 8 February 2020. In February, the Government evacuated 645 people from Wuhan and placed them in quarantine at two centres. These measures reflected an approach based on early risk assessment, surveillance and coordination rather than waiting for infections to spread before building response mechanisms. Clear mandates: Establishing legal and administrative authority As the outbreak intensified, India strengthened the legal and administrative framework for managing the emergency. On 11 March 2020, powers under the Disaster Management Act, 2005, were delegated to the Union Health Secretary. Two days later, States were advised to invoke the Disaster Management Act and the Epidemic Diseases Act, 1897, wherever necessary. On 29 March 2020, the Government constituted 11 Empowered Groups, each assigned a specific area of responsibility. Their mandates covered the medical response, testing, supply chains, communication, public grievances and other essential aspects of pandemic management. The arrangement was intended to ensure that different parts of the response had clearly defined leadership and responsibilities. Senior officials, including the Union Home Secretary and the Secretary of the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology, led groups dealing with their respective areas. The Government also issued operational plans to guide implementation. The Cluster Containment Plan, released on 2 March, outlined measures for case identification, contact tracing and containment of affected areas. On 4 April, a plan for managing large outbreaks, accompanied by a checklist of district-level actions, was shared with States. On 28 April, the Union Health Secretary wrote to all Chief Secretaries, asking them to ensure the continuation of essential medical services. The Group of Ministers overseeing the response reviewed progress, with its 14th meeting on 5 May 2020 hearing presentations from several Empowered Groups....

national_raw_news.title: Forest Rights Act: Recognising rights, securing livelihoods of forest-dwelling communities
national_raw_news.content: The Forest Rights Act, 2006, provides legal recognition to the land and community forest rights of Scheduled Tribes and other traditional forest dwellers. With 25.42 lakh titles distributed across nearly 238 lakh acres, the focus is now on strengthening implementation, linking beneficiaries to livelihood schemes and digitising the claims process. What is the Forest Rights Act? For generations, forest-dwelling communities have lived in forests and depended on them for their homes, food and livelihoods. However, many of their traditional rights over forest land remained unrecorded when forests were consolidated under government control during the colonial period and after Independence. The Scheduled Tribes and Other Traditional Forest Dwellers (Recognition of Forest Rights) Act, 2006, commonly known as the Forest Rights Act (FRA), seeks to address this historical gap. It recognises and vests legal rights over forest land in forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes (FDSTs) and other traditional forest dwellers (OTFDs). The Act received the President’s assent on December 29, 2006, and came into force on December 31, 2007. The Forest Rights Rules were notified on January 1, 2008. The legislation has three broad objectives: recognising forest rights that were not recorded earlier; providing secure land tenure, livelihood and food security to eligible communities; and strengthening forest conservation by giving rights holders the responsibility and authority to use forests sustainably, conserve biodiversity and maintain ecological balance. The Ministry of Tribal Affairs is the nodal ministry for implementing the Act, while State Governments and Union Territory Administrations are responsible for its implementation. The Act is being implemented in 20 States and the Union Territory of Jammu and Kashmir. Who is eligible to claim forest rights? The Act covers two categories of communities: * Forest-dwelling Scheduled Tribes: Members of Scheduled Tribes who primarily reside in forests or forest land and depend on them for their bona fide livelihood needs. * Other traditional forest dwellers: Individuals or communities who have primarily resided in and depended on forests for at least three generations, equivalent to 75 years, before December 13, 2005. The rights apply to forest land occupied before December 13, 2005. For land used for a home or cultivation, an individual claim is limited to the area actually occupied, subject to a maximum of four hectares. The Act covers all categories of forest land, including reserved and protected forests, wildlife sanctuaries and national parks. It also provides that eligible forest dwellers cannot be evicted or removed from the land they occupy until the process of recognising and verifying their rights is complete. The Central Government may also provide for the diversion of small areas of forest land, each measuring less than one hectare, for specified government facilities, subject to a recommendation from the Gram Sabha. These facilities include schools, hospitals, anganwadis, fair price shops, drinking water facilities, minor irrigation canals, roads and community centres. What is a Forest Rights Title? A Forest Rights Title is the official document recording a recognised forest right. It identifies the person or community holding the right, the village concerned, the land or forest area covered and its boundaries. For individual titles, the document is issued in the names of the eligible holders. In the case of a married couple, the title is issued jointly in both names. For a single-headed household, it is registered in the name of the single head of the household. A title is signed on behalf of the State Government by three district-level officers: the Divisional Forest Officer, the District Tribal Welfare Officer and the District Collector. The individual rights holder receives a certified copy, while a community title is issued to the Gram Sabha. Forest rights titles are heritable but cannot be sold or transferred. They provide legal recognition of the rights recorded in them. What kinds of rights does the Act recognise? The Act provides for three broad categories of titles, covering individual land rights, community use rights and community forest management rights. 1. Individual Forest Rights These cover forest land occupied by an eligible individual or family for habitation or self-cultivation, subject to the maximum limit of four hectares. The title records the recognised land rights of the household. 2. Community Forest Rights These recognise the customary rights of a village community over resources...
